question: Is the following claim true? Watson and Crick published the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953.
source: author-written for this project; verified by the author

claims.text: Watson and Crick published their double-helix model of DNA in Nature on April 25, 1953.
The paper's title was 'Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid.'
The 1953 Nature paper is the standard citation for the discovery of the double helix.
Watson and Crick are the authors credited with proposing the double-helix model.
The model relied heavily on X-ray diffraction data, including Franklin's Photo 51 and unpublished measurements used without her knowledge.
Franklin and Wilkins published supporting papers in the same issue, making the discovery collaborative in a broader sense.
Franklin's and Wilkins's contributions complicate the story but do not make the claim false, since the claim only says Watson and Crick published the structure.
The model was a proposal supported by indirect evidence rather than a directly observed structure.
The indirect-evidence objection is just a matter of wording, and the phrase 'published the double-helix structure' is accepted usage.
Authorship, year, and venue all match the historical record, so the claim is true.
